Liam: prepare benchmark harness and sample load script by 2026-04-24

header:
Date: 2026-04-20
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramirez (Redwood SA); Rajiv Menon (Horizon Finance - Head of ML), Tara Li (Platform Engineer), Ana Gutierrez (Product)
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling. Goal: validate Redwood hosted inference for Horizon Finance conversational summarization and risk-detection pipelines. Discussed QPS targets, concurrency, token distributions, benchmark plan, success criteria (latency SLAs, cost per 1M tokens, accuracy/regression), and a 4-6 week POC timeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in 30 seconds, um this is maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account.
[00:12] Rajiv: hey maya, thanks. we've got about 55 minutes, want to use most of it to get to numbers.
[00:22] Liam: quick intro from my side, liam o'connor, i'll own the performance and benchmark side, and sofia will help with architecture constraints.
[00:35] Tara: great \u0014 from horizon side i'm tara, i manage the infra, i'll share traces and our token hist later.
[00:45] Ana: ana here, product, tying POC success to rollout timelines.
[00:50] Maya: perfect, agenda \u0014 workload characterization, target qps and concurrency, what your input/output token shapes look like, then benchmark plan and success metrics, timelines. does that sound right?
[01:05] Rajiv: yes. high level: we have two LLM-powered flows \u0014 chat summarization for customer support tickets, and a short risk-detection classifier that runs on transactions. chat is the heavy token case, risk is low token but high qps.
[01:22] Liam: can you give ballpark numbers for each? qps, concurrency, and token sizes? even approximate helps us size the pilot.
[01:30] Rajiv: sure. summarization: average 60 inbound tokens, output around 180 tokens \u0014 but long tails up to 1,000 tokens on big threads. qps is relatively low steady state 2-4 qps, but concurrency can spike to 20 when we batch ingestion windows after business hours.
[01:50] Tara: for risk detection, it's smaller: input 12-30 tokens, output 8-20 tokens, qps 40 steady, peaks to 120 for minute-long bursts, concurrency ~60 at peak.
[02:10] Ana: our SLOs \u0014 for risk detection we need p95 latency under 200ms ideally, for summarization p95 under 800ms is acceptable but want p50 < 250ms.
[02:24] Liam: okay that's helpful. a couple clarifying questions \u0014 are these calls synchronous (user-facing) or async batch? and do you need streaming for the summarization?
[02:33] Rajiv: chat summarization is user-facing, yes streaming would be nice for perceived latency, but not mandatory. risk detection is sync, we need sub-200ms.
[02:42] Maya: got it. on the infra side, tara, do you prefer hosted api for the pilot or private/vpc? any compliance constraints?
[02:52] Tara: for pilot we can use hosted in our region, but for production we likely need private VPC; we handle PCI scope so any sensitive transaction fields must be redacted, but the pilot can use pseudonymized traces.
[03:05] Sofia: quick note on model choices \u0014 you mentioned summarization and a compact risk model. we typically test with a mid-sized open LLM (13B quantized) for latency baselines and run a higher-quality 70B variant for quality comparisons. quantization and kernel selection will change p95 by factors.
[03:26] Rajiv: that makes sense. cost sensitivity: we have budget constraints so cost per 1M tokens is a key metric for procurement.
[03:34] Liam: our benchmark plan addresses that \u0014 we'll run steady-state and peak replay, measure tokens, egress, and compute cost estimates. we'll include caching/kv prefix hits in the model. any caching on your side?
[03:47] Tara: we do have prefix caching for some templated responses but not for free-text summarization.
[03:54] Liam: okay, then our harness will model both cold and warmed kv cache behavior.
[04:00] Rajiv: how do you recommend we size for concurrency? e.g., risk detection peak concurrency of 60, do you recommend dedicated capacity?
[04:10] Maya: for the risk detection profile \u0014 high sustained qps with low token lengths \u0014 Dedicated capacity is a good fit: predictable throughput and lower cost at scale. Hosted can handle the pilot but Dedicated gives you better p95 guarantees.
[04:21] Tara: procurement will prefer a hosted pilot first. can you put numbers on expected p95 for hosted with 13B-quantized vs 70B?
[04:30] Liam: rough numbers: on a T4/RTX-class serving setup we see p95s around 60-120ms for 13B quantized under small token lengths (~20 tokens out), and 200-350ms for 70B depending on kv cache and batching. for longer outputs like 180 tokens, add roughly 120-300ms depending on batching. those are ballpark, we'll produce concrete numbers from the pilot run.
[04:55] Ana: what's your approach to measuring quality/regression? we need to know the 70B is actually improving downstream metrics.
[05:02] Sofia: we'll run a small eval set of ~500 prompts from your production traces, compare ROUGE/sem-sim scores and include human validation on a sample. we'll tie quality thresholds to the success criteria.
[05:15] Rajiv: success criteria summary: latency SLOs, cost per 1M tokens within our budget, no quality regression vs current baseline, and a plan for private deployment.
[05:25] Maya: can we quantify budget?
[05:27] Rajiv: procurement gave a soft target: under $250 per 1M tokens for the summarization workload with acceptable quality; risk detection is okay up to $50 per 1M tokens since it's low-token.
[05:40] Liam: good, we'll report cost under assumed tokenization and batching. we'll also show effects of enabling KV caching and larger batch sizes.
[05:48] Tara: on token distribution, we'll share histograms \u0014 we usually have a long tail, maybe 5% of requests are >800 tokens. those should be handled gracefully.
[05:58] Maya: for the pilot timeline what does horizon prefer?
[06:01] Ana: want to be able to sign off in 4-6 weeks, ideally faster. we need to show performance and cost with real-ish traffic.
[06:10] Liam: proposed timeline: week 0 (this week) \u0014 share workbook and traces; week 1 \u0014 Redwood runs initial hosted benchmarks with synthetic replay; week 2 \u0014 joint run with your sanitized traces and baseline evaluation; week 3 \u0014 optimization (batching, caching, quantization knob); week 4 \u0014 deliver final report and ops handoff. if you want Dedicated sizing, add 1-2 weeks for capacity planning and dedicated cluster tests.
[06:35] Rajiv: sounds reasonable. what artifacts will you share?
[06:39] Maya: POC workbook (link), benchmark spreadsheet with cost calc (link), sample load scripts, and an ops runbook for private deployment. we'll also share SOC2/security docs for procurement.
[06:51] Tara: procurement will want encryption and KMS details. any gotchas for VPC/private?
[06:56] Sofia: we use customer-managed VPC peering or private link options, also support bring-your-own KMS. we'll attach architecture diagrams. auditing and logs are available for the private plane.
[07:08] Rajiv: for the benchmark harness, can you simulate the bursty peak behavior? our risk detection bursts are very spiky \u0014 short high qps windows.
[07:16] Liam: yes, the load script supports burst windows, constant steady-state, and replay from trace with timestamp preservation. we'll run multiple runs: cold cache, warmed cache, and a peak burst test.
[07:28] Ana: what about functional correctness? for risk detection we need deterministic outputs for given inputs 99% of the time. can you control randomness/temperature?
[07:36] Liam: yep, we'll run tests with temperature=0 and log seeds; also include top-k/top-p configs. model variant parity testing is part of the plan.
[07:46] Tara: on metrics: we'll want p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost breakdown per token.
[07:55] Maya: we'll include those in the benchmark report. also trace-level token breakdown so you can map cost to feature flows.
[08:03] Rajiv: any recommended batch sizes? we don't want batching to add latency for the risk path.
[08:08] Sofia: for low-latency small-token calls, keep batching small (1-4) and prioritize latency SLOs; for summarization batching of 8-16 can improve cost substantially while keeping acceptable tail latency if you allow streaming. We'll include automatic batching configs in the report.
[08:28] Ana: okay. last question \u0014 how do we measure the effect of quantization on quality?
[08:33] Liam: run A/B: quantized 13B vs float 70B and measure your eval metrics plus human sample. if quality gap is unacceptable, we present tradeoffs with cost delta and ops complexity.
[08:46] Maya: recap of next steps: maya to send workbook and pricing, liam to prepare harness and schedule runs, tara to provide traces and sanitized payloads, horizon to confirm pilot scope and internal stakeholders.
[08:58] Rajiv: I'll get traces to tara and we'll upload them by 4/22.
[09:03] Tara: yes will do, expect sanitized CSV and token hist.
[09:07] Ana: schedule the perf run for week of 4/27.
[09:11] Maya: noted, we'll send calendar invite for the perf window and the POC workbook today. thanks all.
[09:16] Rajiv: thanks everyone.
[09:20] [meeting ends]
